question_text: A 67-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because of severe dyspnea and orthopnea for 6 hours. He has a history of congestive heart disease and an ejection fraction of 40%. The medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He appears confused. At the hospital, his blood pressure is 165/110 mm Hg, the pulse is 135/min, the respirations are 48/min, and the temperature is 36.2°C (97.2°F). Crackles are heard at both lung bases. There is pitting edema from the midtibia to the ankle bilaterally. The patient is intubated and admitted to the critical care unit for mechanical ventilation and treatment. Intravenous morphine, diuretics, and nitroglycerine are initiated. Which of the following is the most effective method to prevent nosocomial infection in this patient?
